source_text:
Ἃ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ποιῇ, ὁ πατήρ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ· ταῦτα καὶ οὐχὶ τοιαῦτα, οὐ γὰρ κατὰ μίμησιν ἕτερα
ποιῶ, ἀλλὰ τὰ αὐτὰ ἐργάζομαι ἃ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐργάζεται. Ὅθεν καὶ τὰ ῥήματά μου ἀνατιθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔλεγον· Τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ ὑμῖν ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ λαλῶ· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα. Αὐτῷ δὲ τὰ ἔργα καὶ τὰ ῥήματα ἀνεθέμην, οὐχ ἵνα δείξω ὅτι διακονίαν πληρῶ, ἀλλ' ἵνα δείξω ὅτι οὕτως συνήνωμαι τῷ πατρὶ φύσει, ὡς μήτε λόγον μήτε ἔργον ἄνευ αὐτοῦ ἔχειν. Ὅθεν ἐπήγαγεν λέγων· Πιστεύετέ μοι ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί· εἰ δὲ μή, κἂν διὰ τὰ ἔργα πιστεύετε. Ὥσπερ οὖν ἐκεῖ ἐργαζόμενος ἔλεγον ὅτι Ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα, οὕτως καὶ ὧδε λέγω ὅτι Τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἐκεῖνος ποιεῖ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ· ταῦτα καὶ οὐχὶ τοιαῦτα. Τὸ οὖν Οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν <οὐδὲν> μὴ ἐπαναιρέσει μου τῆς ἐλευθερίας; Νόει· ὅσα γὰρ θέλω ποιεῖν καὶ ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ δύναμαι, ἀλλ' οὐ θέλω· εἰ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ φιλεῖ τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πάντα δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ ἃ αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, πῶς ἐγὼ λάθω τὸν πάντα δι' ἐμοῦ ποιοῦντα; Ποιεῖ δὲ δι' ἐμοῦ οὐχ ὡς δι' ὑπουργοῦ· οὐ γὰρ ὑπουργῶ ἀλλὰ συνεργῶ, οὐ διακονίαν πληρῶν ἀλλὰ αὐθεντίαν ἔχων ἐργάζομαι. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζωοποιεῖ σύνδρομον ἔχων τῇ θελήσει τὴν δύναμιν, οὕτως οὐ διακονίαν πληρῶν νεκροὺς ἐγείρω, ἀλλὰ δυνάμει, αὐθεντίᾳ, ἐξουσίᾳ, θελήσει, ὅτι οὓς ἐγείρω καὶ κρίνω. Ὁ πατὴρ γὰρ οὐ κρίνει οὐδένα· ἀλλ' οὐ διὰ ἀδυναμίαν οὐ κρίνει, ἀλλ' ὅτι τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκεν τῷ υἱῷ· δι' οὗ γὰρ εἰργάσατο, δι' αὐτοῦ καὶ κρίνει. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο δὲ πάντα ποιεῖ, ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσιν τὸν υἱὸν καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν πατέρα. Τότε γὰρ μάλιστα αἰσθάνεται τίμης, ὅταν ἴδῃ τὸν ἐξ αὐτοῦ θεοπρεπῶς τιμώμενον υἱόν· ὁ μὴ τιμῶν τὸν υἱὸν οὐ τιμᾷ τὸν πατέρα τὸν πέμψαντα αὐτόν, οὐ γὰρ δέχεται τιμὴν ἐπ' ἀτιμίᾳ υἱοῦ. Ἔπεμψέ με γὰρ διὰ τὴν σάρκα, οὐχ ἵνα ὑβρισθῶ, ἀλλ' ἵνα δοξασθῶ. Ὅθεν ἐπειδὴ ἀγνωμόνως διετέθητε εἰς ἐμέ, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ δι' αὐτῆς τῆς ἀποσταλείσης σαρκὸς πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔλεγον· Πάτερ, δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν. Σὺ δόξασον ὃν οὗτοι ὑβρίζουσι, σὺ καὶ τὴν ὑπ' αὐτῶν ἀθετουμένην δόξασον σάρκα, ἵνα μάθωσιν ὅτι καὶ τὸν ἐκ Μαρίας ἄνθρωπον διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὸν μονογενῆ σου υἱὸν κοινωνίαν ἀδιακρίτως ὡς πατὴρ δοξάσεις ἐκείνην διδοὺς τῷ ἀναληφθέντι παρ' ἐμοῦ ναῷ νῦν δόξαν, ἣν ἐγὼ αὐτὸς πρὸ αἰώνων παρά σοι ἐκ φύσεως εἶχον ... 3
thought_title: The Son acts with the Father, not as a servant
orientation: Jesus is speaking in the first person, explaining that his works and words are the Father's own, not a subordinate service but a union of nature, will, and authority.
pass_a_gloss: For whatever that one does, the Father, these things also the Son does in the same way; these things and not things of such a kind, for I do not make other things according to imitation, but I work the same things which also the Father works. Whence also, attributing my words to him, I was saying: The words which I speak to you I do not speak from myself; but the Father who remains in me does the works. And I attributed the works and the words to him, not in order that I might show that I fulfill a service, but in order that I might show that I have been united to the Father in nature in this way, so as to have neither word nor work without him. Whence he added, saying: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if not, believe because of the works. Just as therefore there, working, I was saying that The Father who remains in me does the works, so also here I say that The works which that one does, these things also the Son does in the same way; these things and not things of such a kind. Therefore the saying The Son cannot do anything of himself—does it not take away my freedom? Understand: for as many things as I wish to do, I also can do them from myself, but I do not wish to; for if the Father loves the Son and shows him all things which he himself does, how could I escape the notice of the one who does all things through me? And he does through me not as through an underling; for I do not serve as an underling but I work together, not fulfilling a service but having authority I work. For just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, having power running together with his will, so I raise the dead not fulfilling a service, but by power, authority, right, will, because those whom I raise I also judge. For the Father judges no one; but he does not judge because of inability, but because he has given all judgment to the Son; for through whom he worked, through him also he judges. And for this reason he does all things, in order that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. For then especially he perceives honor, when he sees the Son who is from him being honored in a manner befitting God; the one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him, for he does not receive honor upon dishonor of the Son. For he sent me because of the flesh, not in order that I might be insulted, but in order that I might be glorified. Whence since you were disposed ungratefully toward me, for this reason also through the very flesh that was sent I was saying to him: Father, glorify your Son. You glorify the one whom these insult, you also glorify the flesh that is rejected by them, in order that they may learn that also the man from Mary, because of the communion with your only-begotten Son, you will glorify without distinction as Father, giving to the temple taken up from me now the glory which I myself before the ages had from nature with you ...

choices.why: The glossary requires 'in the same way' for ὁμοίως, and the verb ποιεῖ is rendered 'does' to match the Father's action exactly.

choices.english: not things of such a kind
choices.why: The contrast is between the same things (ταῦτα) and merely similar things (τοιαῦτα); 'things of such a kind' preserves the demonstrative force.
The glossary bans 'subordinate role' for διακονίαν; 'fulfill a service' keeps the verb πληρῶ literal and the noun as 'service'.
rejected: I carry out a subordinate role

choices.why: The glossary requires 'work together' for συνεργῶ, distinguishing it from serving under someone.
The glossary requires 'authority' for αὐθεντίᾳ, and the context contrasts it with service.
ὑπουργός means a subordinate worker or servant; 'underling' captures the contrast with working together as an equal.

pass_b_english: For whatever the Father does, the Son also does in the same way. The same things, not merely things of that kind. I do not produce other things by imitation. I work the very things the Father works. That is why I attributed my words to him and said, “The words I speak to you I do not speak of myself; the Father who remains in me does the works” (John 14:10). I attributed the works and the words to him, not to show that I fulfill a service, but to show that I have been united to the Father in nature in such a way that I have neither word nor work without him. That is why I went on to say, “Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if not, believe because of the works” (John 14:11; John 5:36). Just as there, when I was working, I said, “The Father who remains in me does the works,” so here too I say, “The works that he does, the Son also does in the same way. The same things, not merely things of that kind.”

Christ continues: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom? Understand it this way. Whatever I wish to do, I can also do of myself, but I do not wish to. For if the Father loves the Son and shows him everything he himself does, how could I escape the notice of the one who does all things through me? And he does them through me, but not as through an underling. I do not serve as an underling; I work together. I do not fulfill a service; I work with authority. For just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, having power that moves together with his will, so I raise the dead not by fulfilling a service, but by power, authority, right, and will. Those I raise, I also judge. For the Father judges no one. But he does not refrain from judging because of inability, but because he has given all judgment to the Son. Through the one by whom he worked, through him he also judges.

And he does all things for this reason: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father (John 5:23). For the Father most of all delights in honor when he sees the Son who comes from him honored in a way worthy of God. The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him, for the Father does not accept honor at the cost of the Son’s dishonor.

Christ says: He sent me because of the flesh, not so that I would be insulted, but so that I would be glorified. Therefore, since you were disposed toward me without gratitude, through the very flesh that had been sent I kept saying to the Father, “Father, glorify your Son” (John 17:1). Glorify the one these people insult. Glorify also the flesh they reject, so that they may learn that, as Father, you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction, because of his communion with your only-begotten Son. You will give now to the temple assumed by me, my human body, the glory that I myself had from nature with you before the ages.
notes: The source has a duplicated οὐδὲν in the phrase Οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν <οὐδὲν>; the duplication is marked in the source and likely a scribal error; the gloss renders it once.

problems.quote: John 14:10
problems.source_quote: Τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ ὑμῖν ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ λαλῶ· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα
problems.why: The words quoted match John 5:19b-20a context, not John 14:10. The Johannine verse about 'the Father who remains in me does the works' in this exact form belongs to John 5, not 14.
problems.fix: John 5:19
problems.ruling: Quote is from John 5:19‑20, not John 14:10; mis‑attributing scripture misleads readers.

problems.quote: John 10:38
problems.source_quote: Πιστεύετέ μοι ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί· εἰ δὲ μή, κἂν διὰ τὰ ἔργα πιστεύετε
problems.why: The words quoted match John 14:10-11, not John 10:38. John 10:38 has 'believe the works' but lacks 'I am in the Father and the Father is in me' formula.
problems.ruling: Formula belongs to John 14:10‑11, not John 10:38; wrong citation changes source.

problems.quote: I spoke through the very flesh that had been sent
problems.source_quote: δι' αὐτῆς τῆς ἀποσταλείσης σαρκὸς πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔλεγον
problems.why: The Greek says 'through the very flesh that had been sent to him [the Father] I was saying.' The English 'that had been sent' lacks 'to him' (πρὸς αὐτὸν = to the Father), and 'I spoke' for ἔλεγον misses the imperfect 'I was saying/kept saying.' More importantly, 'the flesh that had been sent' — but the flesh was not 'sent to the Father'; rather, Jesus speaks to the Father through the flesh that was sent (i.e., the incarnate flesh). Actually πρὸς αὐτὸν goes with ἔλεγον: 'I was saying to him.' So: 'through the very flesh that had been sent, to him I was saying.' The English misattaches 'to him' to 'sent' rather than 'saying.'
problems.fix: through the very flesh that had been sent, to him I kept saying
problems.ruling: Missing ‘to him’ and tense alters who is addressed and the ongoing nature of the speech.

problems.quote: the temple taken up from me
problems.why: ἀναληφθέντι means 'taken up' but in context of incarnation refers to the flesh/body 'assumed' by the Son. 'Taken up from me' suggests the temple was taken up/exalted from Jesus, rather than the body assumed by him. 'Assumed by me' or 'taken on by me' is the theological sense.
problems.fix: the temple assumed by me
problems.ruling: ‘taken up from me’ reverses direction; should be ‘taken up by me’ (assumed), changing meaning.

problems.quote: giving now to the temple taken up from me the glory that I myself had from nature with you before the ages
problems.source_quote: ἐκείνην διδοὺς τῷ ἀναληφθέντι παρ' ἐμοῦ ναῷ νῦν δόξαν, ἣν ἐγὼ αὐτὸς πρὸ αἰώνων παρά σοι ἐκ φύσεως εἶχον
problems.why: The syntax is mangled. 'ἐκείνην...δόξαν' = 'that glory' (accusative with διδούς). 'giving now to the temple...that glory, which I myself had...' The English puts 'now' after 'temple' making it sound temporal, but νῦν modifies διδούς ('now giving'). Also 'from nature with you' for ἐκ φύσεως παρά σοι — 'by nature from you' or 'from you by nature' would be better. 'With you' suggests accompaniment rather than origin.
problems.fix: now giving to the temple assumed by me that glory which I myself had from you by nature before the ages
problems.ruling: Sentence order and phrasing misrepresent the clause, obscuring who gives what glory and when.

edits.old: I spoke through the very flesh that had been sent, saying to him,
edits.new: through the very flesh that had been sent, to him I kept saying,

edits.old: the temple taken up from me
giving now to the temple taken up from me the glory that I myself had from nature with you before the ages
edits.new: now giving to the temple assumed by me that glory which I myself had from you by nature before the ages

fixed: John 14:10 → John 5:19: The quoted words match John 5:19b-20a context, not John 14:10.
John 10:38 → John 14:10-11: The quoted words match John 14:10-11, not John 10:38.

I spoke through the very flesh that had been sent → through the very flesh that had been sent, to him I kept saying: πρὸς αὐτὸν goes with ἔλεγον, and the imperfect is better rendered as 'kept saying.'
the temple taken up from me → the temple assumed by me: ἀναληφθέντι in this context means 'assumed' by the Son, not 'taken up from' him.

giving now to the temple taken up from me the glory that I myself had from nature with you before the ages → now giving to the temple assumed by me that glory which I myself had from you by nature before the ages: νῦν modifies διδούς, and ἐκ φύσεως παρά σοι means 'from you by nature,' not 'from nature with you.'

problems.quote: John 5:19
problems.source_quote: Τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ ὑμῖν ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ λαλῶ· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ὁ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα
problems.why: The words quoted match John 14:10, not John 5:19.
problems.fix: John 14:10
problems.ruling: Greek quote matches John 14:10, not John 5:19 as cited.

problems.source_quote: Πιστεύετέ μοι ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί· εἰ δὲ μή, κἂν διὰ τὰ ἔργα πιστεύετε
problems.why: The words quoted match John 14:11 and John 5:36, not John 14:10-11 as a unit; first clause is John 14:11, second is John 5:36.
problems.fix: John 14:11; John 5:36
problems.ruling: Quote spans John 14:11‑12; citation of John 14:10‑11 (and John 5:36) is incorrect.

problems.quote: So does “the Son cannot do anything of himself” take away my freedom?
problems.source_quote: Τὸ οὖν Οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ ... μὴ ἐπαναιρέσει μου τῆς ἐλευθερίας;
problems.why: Greek asks if it will NOT take away freedom; English asks if it does take away, reversing the negation.
problems.fix: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom?
problems.ruling: Greek μὴ ἐπαναιρέσει is 'will it not take away'; English 'does...take away' loses the negation, changing meaning.

edits.old: So does “the Son cannot do anything of himself” take away my freedom?
edits.new: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom?

fixed: Changed John 5:19 to John 14:10: the quoted words match John 14:10.
Changed John 14:10-11 to John 14:11; John 5:36: first clause is John 14:11, second is John 5:36.
Restored the negation: Greek asks if it will not take away freedom.

problems.quote: That is why he went on to say
problems.why: The subject of ἐπήγαγεν is Jesus (continuing from the first person discourse), but 'he went on to say' makes it unclear who 'he' is. Given the context has Jesus speaking in first person ('I attributed... I said'), shifting to 'he' is confusing. The Greek has Jesus continuing to speak; the English should maintain 'I went on to say' or clarify.
problems.fix: That is why I went on to say
problems.ruling: Greek speaker is Jesus (first person); English shifts to ‘he’, confusing attribution.

problems.quote: because those I raise, I also judge
problems.why: ὅτι here is not 'because' but introduces the content of what precedes—'that those I raise, I also judge' or 'namely, those I raise, I judge.' The 'because' makes it seem like the reason for the power/authority, when it's actually specifying what the power consists in. This changes the logic.
problems.fix: namely, those I raise, I also judge
problems.ruling: ‘because’ adds causal nuance absent in Greek; alters logical relation.

problems.quote: you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction as Father
problems.why: The syntax is mangled. 'without distinction as Father' should go with 'you will glorify'—'you will glorify without distinction as Father.' The English makes it seem like 'the man from Mary without distinction as Father' which is nonsense. The word order needs fixing: 'as Father, you will glorify without distinction.'
problems.fix: so that they may learn that, as Father, you will glorify the man from Mary without hesitation
problems.ruling: English misplaces ‘without distinction as Father’, making phrase nonsensical; changes intended meaning.

edits.old: That is why he went on to say
edits.new: That is why I went on to say

edits.old: because those I raise, I also judge
edits.new: namely, those I raise, I also judge

edits.old: so that they may learn that you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction as Father, because of his communion with your only-begotten Son
edits.new: so that they may learn that, as Father, you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction, because of his communion with your only-begotten Son

fixed: Changed 'he went on to say' to 'I went on to say' because the Greek ἐπήγαγεν continues Jesus' first-person discourse (Ὅθεν ἐπήγαγεν λέγων).
Changed 'because those I raise, I also judge' to 'namely, those I raise, I also judge' because the Greek ὅτι introduces the content of the preceding clause, not a reason.

Changed 'you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction as Father' to 'as Father, you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction' because the Greek ἀδιακρίτως ὡς πατὴρ δοξάσεις has 'as Father' modifying the verb 'glorify,' not 'the man from Mary.'

problems.quote: the nod of the one commanding directs
problems.why: Four different phrases for the same concept of servile obedience; reader may miss they are synonymous.
problems.fix: Use one consistent term like 'serve as a subordinate' throughout.

variants.text: the nod of the one commanding directs

problems.quote: in the same way
problems.why: Greek hosautos is rendered 'in the same way' but later unpacked as 'same things not similar'; reader may not connect these.
problems.fix: Gloss first occurrence: 'in the same way (the same things, not merely similar ones)'.

variants.text: the same things, not things of such a kind
the very things the Father works

problems.quote: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom?
problems.why: Sudden first-person 'my freedom' after third-person exposition; speaker unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Christ asks: Does this statement not take away my freedom?'

problems.quote: the Father most of all perceives honor
problems.why: 'Perceives' is weak for Greek aisthanetai; suggests passive reception rather than active delight.
problems.fix: Use 'receives' or 'takes pleasure in'.

problems.quote: John 14:11; John 5:36
problems.why: The words quoted ('Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if not, believe because of the works') match John 14:11 but not John 5:36, which has different wording.
problems.fix: Remove John 5:36 or note it as parallel concept, not exact wording.

problems.quote: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom?
problems.why: First person 'my freedom' is Christ's voice but no speaker marker; reader may lose track.
problems.fix: Mark that Christ continues speaking: 'Christ continues: Does the statement...'

problems.quote: He sent me because of the flesh, not so that I would be insulted
problems.why: Christ's first-person voice continues without clear marker after a brief authorial aside.
problems.fix: Add 'Christ says: ' before this sentence.

problems.quote: having power running together with his will
problems.why: Same odd phrase 'running together with'; reads like word-for-word gloss.
problems.fix: Use 'concurring with his will' or 'accompanying his will.'

problems.quote: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if not, believe because of the works" (John 14:11; John 5:36)
problems.why: John 5:36 does not match the quoted words; it says 'the works the Father gave me to accomplish.'
problems.fix: Remove John 5:36 or cite it separately for a different allusion.

problems.quote: Therefore, since you were disposed toward me without gratitude, through the very flesh that had been sent, to him I kept saying
problems.why: Pronoun 'him' and 'I' are ambiguous; Christ speaks but 'him' = Father, and the sentence is convoluted.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'to the Father I kept saying'.

problems.quote: you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction, because of his communion with your only-begotten Son
problems.why: 'Without distinction' is unclear; does it mean 'without hesitation' or 'making no distinction'?
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'you will glorify the man from Mary as one with your only-begotten Son.'

edits.new: the Father most of all receives honor

Speaker marker already added in previous edit.

fixed.quote: he does not judge because of inability; he does not judge because he has given all judgment to the Son
fixed.fix: he does not refrain from judging because of inability, but because he has given all judgment to the Son
fixed.note: As written, the English states that inability is why the Father does not judge, which reverses the Greek's 'not because of inability, but because'.

variants.text: the nod of the one commanding directs

notes.why: Four different phrases for the same concept of servile obedience; reader may miss they are synonymous.
notes.fix: Use one consistent term like 'serve as a subordinate' throughout.

variants.text: the same things, not things of such a kind
the very things the Father works

notes.why: Greek hosautos is rendered 'in the same way' but later unpacked as 'same things not similar'; reader may not connect these.
notes.fix: Gloss first occurrence: 'in the same way (the same things, not merely similar ones)'.

notes.quote: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom?
notes.why: Sudden first-person 'my freedom' after third-person exposition; speaker unclear.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'Christ asks: Does this statement not take away my freedom?'

notes.quote: the Father most of all perceives honor
notes.why: 'Perceives' is weak for Greek aisthanetai; suggests passive reception rather than active delight.
The words quoted ('Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if not, believe because of the works') match John 14:11 but not John 5:36, which has different wording.
notes.fix: Remove John 5:36 or note it as parallel concept, not exact wording.

notes.quote: Does the statement that the Son cannot do anything of himself not take away my freedom?
notes.why: First person 'my freedom' is Christ's voice but no speaker marker; reader may lose track.
notes.fix: Mark that Christ continues speaking: 'Christ continues: Does the statement...'

notes.quote: He sent me because of the flesh, not so that I would be insulted
notes.why: Christ's first-person voice continues without clear marker after a brief authorial aside.

notes.quote: having power running together with his will
notes.why: Same odd phrase 'running together with'; reads like word-for-word gloss.
notes.fix: Use 'concurring with his will' or 'accompanying his will.'

notes.why: 'Temple' here means Christ's human body, but this is not clear to a modern reader.
notes.fix: Add 'temple' means his assumed human body.

notes.quote: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if not, believe because of the works" (John 14:11; John 5:36)
notes.why: John 5:36 does not match the quoted words; it says 'the works the Father gave me to accomplish.'
notes.fix: Remove John 5:36 or cite it separately for a different allusion.

notes.quote: Therefore, since you were disposed toward me without gratitude, through the very flesh that had been sent, to him I kept saying
notes.why: Pronoun 'him' and 'I' are ambiguous; Christ speaks but 'him' = Father, and the sentence is convoluted.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'to the Father I kept saying'.

notes.quote: you will glorify the man from Mary without distinction, because of his communion with your only-begotten Son
notes.why: 'Without distinction' is unclear; does it mean 'without hesitation' or 'making no distinction'?
notes.fix: Rephrase: 'you will glorify the man from Mary as one with your only-begotten Son.'
